Updated August 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

We're improving the Viva Engage experience in Microsoft Teams for iOS by bringing pinned resources and related communities into the Teams mobile app. Pinned resources highlight important links and files within a community, while related communities help users discover other relevant Viva Engage communities. These are two separate features that work together to improve information access and community discovery.

This update aligns the iOS experience with Engage on the web, the Engage mobile app, and Teams for Android, helping users discover important content and related communities more easily—especially those who rely on Teams on iOS as their primary communication tool.

This message is associated with Roadmap ID 559107.

When this will happen:

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-June 2026 (previously late May) and is expected to complete by end of September 2026 (previously mid-August).

How this affects your organization:

Who is affected:

  • Users who access Viva Engage communities in Microsoft Teams on iOS
  • Community admins who manage Viva Engage communities

What will happen:

  • Users will see pinned resources for a community directly within Teams on iOS.
  • Users will see related communities surfaced within the community experience.

  • The experience will match what is already available in the Viva Engage mobile app, Viva Engage on the web, and Teams for Android.
  • The feature is enabled by default.
  • There are no changes to existing admin policies or configurations.

What you can do to prepare:

No admin action is required.

  • Communicate this update to end users who use Teams on iOS.
  • Encourage Viva Engage community admins to review pinned resources and related communities.
  • Update internal documentation or helpdesk guidance, if applicable.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Viva Engage in Microsoft Teams for iOS will add pinned resources and related communities from mid-June to September 2026, aligning with other platforms. Users and community admins will see these features by default with no admin changes needed. Communication and documentation updates are recommended.

Details.Name: Platforms
Details.Value: iOS

Title: Viva Engage: Pinned resources and related communities in Teams for iOS

Body.Content:
What and Why:

To help protect Microsoft Teams users from spam, phishing, and other abusive activity, Microsoft is introducing outbound external messaging limits for organizations that use only the default Microsoft Online Email Routing Address (MOERA) domain, such as contoso.onmicrosoft.com.

These limits are designed to reduce large-scale abuse while preserving normal collaboration scenarios. Most organizations using Teams for standard business communications are not expected to reach these limits.

Rollout Schedule:

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-September 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-September 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected

Organizations that use only the default onmicrosoft.com domain and have not configured a custom domain.

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External chat and messaging

What will happen

  • Outbound Teams messages sent to external users will be subject to messaging limits intended to reduce abusive or high-volume activity.
  • When an applicable limit is reached, users may be temporarily unable to send messages to external users.
  • Users will see an in-product notification indicating that outbound external messaging has been temporarily limited.
  • Internal Teams messaging and collaboration within your organization will not be affected.
  • External messaging capabilities will automatically resume when activity falls below the applicable threshold.

The protection is enabled by default and does not require administrator configuration.

An optional administrator alert for throttling events will become available after the initial rollout. This post will be updated when information about enabling the alert is available.

Action Required / Recommendations:

If your organization relies on the default onmicrosoft.com domain for production use, review your domain configuration before rollout.

  • Verify whether your organization uses only the default onmicrosoft.com domain.
  • If appropriate, add and configure a custom domain for your Microsoft 365 organization.
  • Inform help desk personnel and Teams administrators that users may encounter temporary outbound external messaging restrictions if applicable limits are reached.
  • Review the Teams limits and specifications documentation for additional guidance.

No action is required for organizations that already have a custom domain configured.

Additional Information

This change helps reduce spam and other abusive activity originating from tenants that use only the default onmicrosoft.com domain while maintaining normal collaboration experiences for legitimate users.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Teams will impose outbound external messaging limits starting mid-September 2026 for organizations using only the default onmicrosoft.com domain to reduce spam and abuse. Limits may temporarily block external messages but won't affect internal communication. Admins should consider adding a custom domain and prepare support staff.

Title: External messaging limits for onmicrosoft.com-only organizations in Microsoft Teams

Body.Content:
What and why:

Microsoft is introducing organizational skills support for Copilot in PowerPoint. These reusable skills can help users apply organization-specific guidance when working with Copilot in PowerPoint for the web, PowerPoint desktop for Windows, and PowerPoint for Mac.

Tenant admins will be able to add and share organizational skills through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Rollout schedule:

Frontier: We will begin rolling out in end of August 2026 and expect to complete by early September 2026.

Impact on your organization:

Who is affected: 

  • M365 admins and eligible users of Copilot in PowerPoint.

Platforms:

  • PowerPoint for the web
  • PowerPoint desktop for Windows
  • PowerPoint for Mac

After this rollout:

  • Tenant admins will be able to add and share organizational skills for Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • Shared skills will provide users with reusable, organization-specific guidance when they use Copilot in supported PowerPoint experiences.
  • Tenant admins will manage these skills through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Users will be able to access shared organizational skills in PowerPoint for the web, PowerPoint desktop for Windows, and PowerPoint for Mac.

Action Required / Recommendations:

No action is required before the rollout.

If your organization plans to use shared organizational skills:

  • Identify the tenant admins who will manage the skills.
  • Determine which organizational skills should be available to PowerPoint users.
  • Establish an internal process for creating, reviewing, approving, publishing, and maintaining shared skills.
  • Update your internal user guidance and support materials for Copilot in PowerPoint as appropriate.
  • Ensure eligible users have access to supported PowerPoint experiences and meet the applicable Microsoft 365 Copilot requirements.
  • Review Deploy Organization skills for Copilot in PowerPoint

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft will roll out organizational skills support for Copilot in PowerPoint (web, Windows, Mac) by early September 2026. Tenant admins can add and manage reusable, organization-specific skills via the Microsoft 365 admin center, enhancing user guidance without requiring pre-rollout action.

Title: Organization skills support in Copilot for PowerPoint (Frontier release)

Body.Content:
Updated August 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction:

Microsoft Edge for Business will soon support summarization and contextual grounding with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. This enhancement enables users to ask Copilot questions about multiple open browser tabs, Microsoft 365 documents (such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint), and YouTube videos directly from the Edge side pane.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 496364, 499423, and 499424.

When this will happen:

  • General Availability (Multiple browser tabs and YouTube videos): Currently Available
  • General Availability (Microsoft 365 documents): Rollout is expected to begin mid-September 2026 (previously end of August)

How this affects your organization:

Who is affected: Users signed in to Microsoft Edge for Business with their Entra ID and who have access to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to ask Copilot questions about open browser tabs, Microsoft 365 documents, and YouTube videos.
  • The feature will be off by default.
  • If Copilot is restricted from accessing page content via Data Loss Prevention (DLP) or the EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext policy, it will be suppressed to maintain DLP integrity.
  • Existing DLP and policy configurations will be respected.

What you can do to prepare:

  • This rollout will happen automatically by the specified date; no admin action is required before rollout.
  • Ensure users who need this capability have access to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
  • Ensure your tenant is configured to support Microsoft 365 Copilot and that eligible users meet all licensing prerequisites, including Entra ID sign-in and applicable Microsoft 365 service plans.
  • Review your current DLP and Edge policy configurations to determine potential impact.
  • Notify users about this upcoming capability.
  • Update internal documentation if needed.

Learn more:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Edge and Access to Page Content | Microsoft Edge | Microsoft Learn
  • Microsoft Edge - Policies | Microsoft Edge | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations:

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Microsoft 365 Copilot introduces contextual grounding and summarization using generative AI across browser tabs, Microsoft 365 documents, and YouTube videos.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can now ask Copilot questions about open browser tabs and documents directly from the Edge sidepane, enabling real-time summarization and contextual responses.
Does the change modify Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies or enforcement?Yes. If DLP or the EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext policy restricts access, Copilot will be suppressed from accessing page content to maintain DLP integrity.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can manage access to Copilot’s contextual grounding capabilities via DLP settings and Edge policy configurations, which can be scoped using Entra ID group membership.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Edge for Business now supports Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat for summarization and contextual grounding across browser tabs, Microsoft 365 documents, and YouTube videos. The feature is off by default, respects DLP and policy settings, and requires Entra ID sign-in and appropriate licensing. Rollout begins mid-September 2026.

Details.Name: Platforms
Details.Value: Web

Title: Microsoft Edge: Microsoft 365 Copilot will support summarization and contextual grounding

Body.Content:
Updated August 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why

As first announced on July 1st, automated investigation and response (AIR) for Defender for Endpoint will no longer run as a separate investigation experience or be available for manual triggering in Microsoft Defender.

There is no change to AIR functionality in Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

The protection capabilities of AIR are already embedded within Microsoft Defender’s always-on antivirus protection stack today. Detection and response run automatically as part of default protection, without requiring a separate investigation workflow.

This change is part of our ongoing “shift left” effort to lift the onus of protection from customers by automating detection and response processes, helping ensure consistent outcomes across endpoints without reliance on a separate, manually initiated investigation experience.

With this update, the standalone AIR investigation experience is removed. For on-demand investigations, teams can run full antivirus scans as needed.

Rollout Schedule

  • Transition (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning and completing in early September 2026

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected

  • Admins and security teams using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Microsoft Defender XDR

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint across supported platforms

What will happen

  • Manual triggering of automated investigation and response (AIR) will no longer be available.
  • AIR will no longer run as a separate investigation experience.
  • Detection and response will occur automatically as part of always-on antivirus protection.
  • Full antivirus scans replace manual AIR investigations for on-demand analysis.
  • Any playbooks, scripts, or integrations that initiate AIR will stop working after September 1, 2026, and must be updated before that date.
  • Protection remains enabled by default.

Action Required / Recommendations

If you are not using AIR manually or through automation, no action is required to maintain protection.

Action is required for organizations using AIR in playbooks, scripts, or integrations, as these will no longer function after September 1, 2026.

  • Review and update any playbooks, scripts, or integrations that initiate AIR before September 1, 2026.
  • Replace AIR-based workflows with full antivirus scan workflows for on-demand investigations.
  • Update internal documentation that references AIR investigations.
  • Inform security and helpdesk teams of this change.

Learn more: 

  • Microsoft Defender Antivirus full scan considerations and best practices | Microsoft Defender for Endpoint | Microsoft Defender | Microsoft Learn
  • Overview of automated investigations | Microsoft Defender for Endpoint | Microsoft Defender | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. AIR will no longer appear as a distinct investigation type, which may affect monitoring and reporting workflows.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint will remove manual triggering and the standalone experience of automated investigation and response (AIR) by early September 2026. AIR functions are integrated into always-on antivirus protection. Organizations using AIR in playbooks or scripts must update them before September 1, 2026.

Title: Microsoft Defender: Automated investigation and response (AIR) integrated into antivirus with manual triggering removed

Body.Content:
What and why:

We’re introducing Create interactive slides in PowerPoint for Windows and Mac. This capability helps users create interactive, full-slide visuals that explain complex concepts, timelines, comparisons, systems, and data.

By making sophisticated visual communication easier to create directly in PowerPoint, this experience can help users communicate ideas more clearly and create engaging presentations with less manual effort.

Rollout schedule:

  • Frontier (Worldwide):
    • Desktop: Available now.
    • Mac: Rolling out now and expected to complete by early September 2026.

Impact on your organization:

Who is affected:

  • PowerPoint for Windows and Mac users who have access to this capability.

Platforms:

  • PowerPoint for Windows and Mac.

After the feature becomes available, eligible users will be able to use Create interactive slides to produce full-slide visual experiences for scenarios such as:

  • Explaining complex concepts.
  • Presenting timelines.
  • Comparing options or information.
  • Illustrating systems and relationships.
  • Communicating data visually.

Organizations participating in the Microsoft Copilot Frontier program can evaluate the preview experience before general availability. Frontier capabilities are pre-release experiences and may change before reaching general availability.

Action required / recommendations:

No action is required before rollout.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review this information with presentation support, adoption, training, and help desk teams.
  • Consider identifying Frontier participants who can evaluate the capability and provide feedback before general availability.
  • Update internal PowerPoint guidance or training materials if your organization maintains standardized presentation-creation processes.
  • Review the Microsoft Copilot Frontier program documentation: Get started with the Microsoft Copilot Frontier Program.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: PowerPoint's new "Create interactive slides" feature (Windows and Mac) enables users to easily create full-slide visuals for complex concepts, timelines, comparisons, systems, and data. Available now on Windows and rolling out on Mac by September 2026, it requires no pre-rollout action but recommends admin review and training updates.

Title: Create interactive slides in PowerPoint with Copilot skill (Windows and Mac)

Updated August 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

To streamline and modernize reporting experiences across Microsoft 365, we are retiring the Outlook for Windows Usage Report in the Exchange admin center (EAC). Admins can continue accessing Outlook usage information in the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC), which offers a more complete and up‑to‑date reporting experience across Microsoft 365 apps.

When this will happen

  • Retirement will begin in early November 2026 (previously mid-August).
  • Retirement will complete in late November 2026 (previously mid-September).

How this affects your organization

Who is affected

  • Admins who use the Exchange admin center (EAC) to view Outlook for Windows usage data.

What will happen

  • The Outlook for Windows Usage Report will be removed from the EAC.
  • No replacement Outlook usage reporting will remain in the EAC after this retirement.
  • Admins can continue accessing Outlook for Windows usage insights through the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC): Reports > Usage > M365 Apps > Usage > Outlook for Windows
  • MAC provides consolidated usage reporting with charts and tables to help admins understand usage patterns across Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.
  • No impact to Outlook for Windows functionality for users.
  • This report retirement will occur automatically; no opt‑out or admin toggle will be available.

What you can do to prepare

  • No admin action is required.
  • If your organization references the EAC usage report in documentation or internal processes, update those materials before the retirement is complete.

Learn more: Microsoft 365 Reports in the admin center - Microsoft 365 Apps usage | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: The Outlook for Windows Usage Report in the Exchange admin center will retire from early to late November 2026. Admins must use the Microsoft 365 admin center for Outlook usage insights. No impact on Outlook functionality; no admin action required, but update any related documentation.

Title: Outlook for Windows report retirement in the Exchange admin center

Body.Content:
Updated August 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft is enhancing the signature editing experience in Outlook for iOS and Android by allowing users to insert images into email signatures directly from OneDrive, in addition to selecting images from their device photo library. This improvement makes it easier for users to access and use signature images stored in OneDrive while maintaining existing organizational data-sharing policies.

Rollout schedule

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in late September 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users of Outlook for iOS and Android who create or edit email signatures

Platforms and services

  • Outlook for iOS
  • Outlook for Android

What will happen

  • Users will see a new option when inserting an image into an email signature: 

  • Selecting Insert image in the signature editor will present:
    • Choose from files to browse and select image files that are stored in OneDrive.
    • Choose from photo library to select an image from the device, which remains the existing behavior.
  • This change is only visible in Outlook for iOS and Android when editing email signatures. Users can select images stored in OneDrive, but there are no changes to the OneDrive application experience.
  • Available OneDrive accounts are determined by your organization's existing cross-account data-sharing policies.
  • The file picker displays only image files.
  • Users can switch between grid and list views while browsing images.
  • Selected images are downloaded and embedded into the signature, consistent with the current behavior for locally stored images.
  • Existing signatures are not modified.
  • The feature is enabled by default and does not require administrator configuration.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. The update is enabled automatically.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform helpdesk and support staff about the updated signature image selection experience.
  • Update internal training materials or screenshots if they reference the signature editor workflow.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Starting late September to late October 2026, Outlook for iOS and Android will let users insert signature images from OneDrive as well as device photo libraries. This feature is enabled by default, requires no admin setup, and respects existing organizational data-sharing policies. No action is needed.

Title: Microsoft Outlook for iOS and Android: Insert signature images from OneDrive

Body.Content:
Updated August 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

We're improving the OneDrive integration with the Apple Files app on iOS to provide a more reliable file experience, including clearer upload status and progress indicators.

As part of this update, OneDrive Shared and SharePoint Libraries locations that users can access only with read-only permissions will no longer appear in the Apple Files app. Users will continue to have access to this content through the OneDrive mobile app.

Users who want to access shared content and libraries in the Apple Files app can use Add to OneDrive. Content added to OneDrive will continue to appear in the Apple Files app and can be edited when users have the appropriate permissions.

Rollout Schedule:

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-August 2026 and is expected to complete by early November 2026 (previously mid-September).

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected

  • Users who access OneDrive shared content or SharePoint libraries through the Apple Files app on iOS devices.

Platforms and Services

  • OneDrive for iOS
  • Apple Files app on iOS
  • SharePoint Online libraries

What will happen

  • Read-only shared locations and library locations will no longer appear in the Apple Files app.
  • Users will continue to be able to access this content in the OneDrive mobile app.
  • Users can use Add to OneDrive to continue accessing shared content and libraries from the Apple Files app.
  • Content added to OneDrive will remain available through the Apple Files app.
  • Users with the required permissions will continue to be able to edit content added to OneDrive.

Action Required / Recommendations:

No admin action is required.

We recommend informing users who access shared content or SharePoint libraries through the Apple Files app on iOS that:

  • Read-only shared and library locations will no longer appear in the Apple Files app after this rollout.
  • They can continue accessing this content through the OneDrive mobile app.
  • They can use Add to OneDrive if they want content to appear in the Apple Files app.

Compliance Considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: OneDrive integration with Apple Files on iOS is improved for reliability and clearer upload status. Read-only shared and SharePoint library locations will no longer appear in Apple Files but remain accessible via the OneDrive app. Users can use "Add to OneDrive" to access and edit content in Apple Files. Rollout: mid-August to early November 2026. No admin action required.

Title: Improved OneDrive experience in Apple Files app

Body.Content:
What and why:

We are updating profile cards in Microsoft Teams to display existing Awards and Certifications profile properties from the Microsoft 365 profile schema. This feature previously rolled out to Outlook and the Microsoft 365 Copilot app in April 2026 and will now be available in Teams profile cards.

Rollout schedule:

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by early October 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early-October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-October 2026.

Impact on your organization:

Who is affected:

  • All users in organizations that populate the Awards and Certifications properties in Microsoft 365 profiles.

What will happen:

  • A new Awards and Certifications section will be added to profile cards in Teams in the Overview and Contact tabs, below the Skills section.
  • Each award or certification entry will display the title and issuer by default. Selecting a badge will reveal additional details, including the description and award date.
  • If your organization does not currently populate these profile properties, no changes will be visible and the new section will not appear on profile cards.

Platforms and services:

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Outlook
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot app
  • Microsoft 365 profile cards

Action required / Recommendations:

  • Review your organization's Microsoft 365 profile data and determine whether the Awards and Certifications properties are populated for users. Values stored in these fields will become visible on profile cards in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • If your organization already uses the Awards and Certifications fields in the Microsoft 365 profile schema, no action is required.
  • Note that the profile card experience is read-only. Users cannot create, edit, or manage awards and certifications directly from the profile card.
  • Review the support documentation: View awards and certification badges on your profile card.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Teams profile cards will display existing Awards and Certifications from Microsoft 365 profiles starting October 2026. This read-only feature shows titles, issuers, and details on badges if populated. No changes appear if these properties are empty. Review your organization's profile data accordingly.

Details.Name: Platforms
Details.Value: Desktop, Mac

Title: Badges on profile cards in Teams

Body.Content:
What and Why:

To help ensure optimal performance, reliability, and security, Outlook for iOS is updating its minimum supported operating system requirements. Following the release of iOS 27, Outlook for iOS will support only the two most recent versions of iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS. This change aligns with Microsoft’s commitment to supporting the latest Apple platforms.

Rollout schedule:

  • Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will begin rolling out in mid-September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

Impact on your organization:

Who is affected

Users accessing Outlook on iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch devices running operating system versions that will no longer be supported.

Platforms and services

  • Outlook for iOS
  • iOS
  • iPadOS
  • watchOS

What will happen

After iOS 27 becomes generally available:

  • Outlook for iOS will no longer receive updates on devices running iOS 18 or earlier.
  • Users on iOS 18 can continue using the last supported version of Outlook. However, over time, the app may stop syncing email and calendar data.
  • Support for iPadOS 18 and watchOS 11 will also end.
  • Supported versions will include iOS 26 and iOS 27, iPadOS 26 and iPadOS 27, and watchOS 26 and watchOS 27.
  • This change does not affect users running iOS 26 or later.

Action required / Recommendations:

  • Review your mobile device inventory and identify devices running operating system versions that will no longer be supported.
  • Notify affected users of the upcoming operating system requirement changes.
  • Encourage users to upgrade eligible devices to iOS 26 or later before the rollout begins. This will help users continue receiving Outlook updates and avoid potential service interruptions.
  • Review options for devices that cannot be upgraded to a supported operating system version.
  • Update your internal support documentation and user communications as appropriate.

No Microsoft 365 admin configuration changes are required for this update.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Outlook for iOS will require iOS 26 or later starting mid-September 2026, supporting only the two latest iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS versions. Users on older versions may lose updates and syncing. Organizations should identify affected devices, notify users, and encourage OS upgrades. No admin changes needed.

Title: Outlook for iOS: Minimum system requirements updated to iOS 26 and above

Body.Content:
What and why:

The Admin app is an application built to help very small businesses manage administrative tasks directly in Teams, Outlook and Microsoft365.com.  Starting in October 2026, the Admin app will no longer be supported or available.

Rollout schedule:

We will begin rolling out mid-August 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

Impact on your organization:

  • Who is affected?
    • Admins using the Admin app in Teams, Outlook or Microsoft365.com
  • What will happen?
    • Starting in August 2026 the Admin app will no longer be pre-pinned or pre-installed in Teams for new very small business admins. Admins will still be able to access the application if it is installed in Teams. 
    • Starting in October 2026 the Admin app will no longer be supported or available to customers in Teams, Outlook, or Microsoft365.com.

Required Action / Recommendations:

  • Admins can continue to use Microsoft Admin Center and Teams Admin Center to manage their Teams environments.
  • Admins can also use the Microsoft 365 Admin Agent to assist them with administrative tasks

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: The Admin app for very small businesses in Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft365.com will retire by October 2026, with rollout starting August 2026. It will no longer be pre-installed or supported. Admins should use Microsoft Admin Center, Teams Admin Center, or Microsoft 365 Admin Agent instead.

Title: Admin app retiring in Teams, Outlook and Microsoft365.com

Body.Content:
What and Why:

We are introducing a new Call Monitor experience in Microsoft Teams for Web that helps users stay connected to meetings while working in other browser tabs. When users move away from an active meeting tab, Teams can display key meeting controls in a separate Picture-in-Picture (PiP) window, making it easier to manage calls and meetings without returning to the meeting tab.

This enhancement improves multitasking during meetings and helps users remain engaged while working elsewhere in their browser.

Rollout Schedule:

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by early October 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

  • Users of Microsoft Teams for Web who join meetings in supported browsers.

Platforms:

  • Teams for Web.

What will happen:

  • Users will receive the new Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Call Monitor experience during Teams meetings.
  • When users navigate away from the active meeting tab, Teams can display meeting controls in a separate PiP window.
  • The PiP Call Monitor helps users remain connected to meetings while working elsewhere in their browser.
  • The experience is available only in browsers that support the required browser capabilities.
  • No changes are required to existing meeting or calling workflows.

Action Required / Recommendations:

No admin action is required before rollout.

  • Ensure helpdesk and support staff are aware of the upcoming user experience change.
  • Review internal training and support materials as needed.
  • Confirm that users are running supported browser versions for Teams for Web.
  • Review Teams for Web prerequisites and supported browsers in Microsoft Learn.

Compliance Considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Teams for Web will introduce a Picture-in-Picture Call Monitor in October 2026, allowing users to manage meeting controls in a separate window while multitasking in other browser tabs. No admin action is needed; users must have supported browsers for this feature.

Details.Name: Platforms
Details.Value: Web

Title: Calls popout into a new window on the browser to support multi-tasking and collaboration during a meeting

Body.Content:
What and why

The September 2026 Windows security update will be released as a standard update rather than a hotpatch update. Some of the security improvements in this update change components that cannot be updated without a restart. As a result, devices enrolled in hotpatching will need to restart to complete installation.

Rollout schedule

  • September 2026: Standard update with restart required for all devices including those that are hotpatch-enabled.
  • October 2026: Planned baseline update month with restart required.
  • November 2026: Next hotpatch update expected.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows Autopatch with hotpatch-enabled devices
  • Users of devices currently enrolled in hotpatch updates

Platforms and services

  • Windows Autopatch
  • Windows 11 hotpatch
  • Windows Server hotpatch

What will happen

  • Hotpatch-enabled devices will require a restart to complete installation of the September 2026 security update.
  • Hotpatch-enabled devices will remain enrolled in hotpatch updates.
  • Devices not using hotpatch updates are unaffected because standard Windows security updates already require a restart.
  • No changes are being made to hotpatch enrollment or configuration requirements.

Action required / recommendations

No action is required.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Inform affected users that a restart will be required following installation of the September 2026 security update.
  • Review maintenance windows and device restart policies to help ensure timely installation.
  • Continue monitoring update deployment and compliance through existing management tools.
  • Track the hotpatch update calendars on the Windows release health site for both Windows 11 and Windows Server. 

Learn more

  • Windows 11 hotpatch calendar - Windows 11 release information | Release health | Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Windows Server hotpatch calendar - Windows Server release information | Windows Search release information | Windows | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance action is required. Update installation and restart behavior will be reflected in update history and compliance reports as usual.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: The September 2026 Windows security update requires a restart for hotpatch-enabled devices because it is a standard update. Devices will remain enrolled in hotpatching, with no changes to enrollment. Administrators should inform users, review restart policies, and monitor updates; no action or compliance changes are needed.

Title: Microsoft Windows Autopatch: September 2026 Windows security update requires a restart for hotpatch-enabled devices

Body.Content:
What and why:

As communicated in MC1454108, beginning in early September, 2026, Microsoft will start redirecting users from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft in organizations where access to copilot.cloud.microsoft is available. Organizations who may have blocked connection to copilot.cloud.microsoft will be redirected in October. To avoid disruption to Copilot access, review your organization's network and security controls to confirm that users can connect to copilot.cloud.microsoft.   

Rollout schedule:

  • In early September, 2026, Microsoft will redirect users from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft in organizations where access to copilot.cloud.microsoft is available.  
  • In early October, 2026 Microsoft will redirect the remaining users who had not been redirected in early September. If your organization cannot complete the required configuration before the redirect, contact your Microsoft account representative to discuss available options. 

Impact on your organization:

When the Copilot web app transitions from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft, users will be automatically redirected. If device, network, proxy, firewall, security gateway, or similar controls block or interfere with the new URL, affected users may be unable to use the Copilot web app. Review these controls and allow the required domain before the redirect begins. 

The redirect remains within the *.cloud.microsoft domain and retains its security, compliance, and enterprise allow-listing properties. Organizations that follow the recommendednetwork configurations for Microsoft 365 Copilot do not need additional network changes. 

Action required / Recommendations:

  • You can validate connectivity to the *.cloud.microsoft domain by using the Microsoft 365 Connectivity Test tool. Use the connectivity tool to validate connectivity to copilot.cloud.microsoft and confirm that your network and security controls allow access before the redirect applies to your organization. If you find out your organization blocks connection to copilot.cloud.microsoft, contact your Microsoft account representative before September 10, 2026 to discuss available options.
  • Confirm that copilot.cloud.microsoft is not blocked in your environment. Review legacy filtering rules, URL category restrictions, proxy policies, firewall rules, tenant restrictions, Conditional Access policies, and app control policies, and update them if needed. 
  • Add *.cloud.microsoft to your organization’s allow lists. If you have questions about tenant-specific network configurations and allow list requirements, you can contact your Microsoft support team for guidance based on your specific environment. Note: Microsoft does not support allowing partial or only selected Microsoft 365 application URLs within the *.cloud.microsoft domain. Allow the entire *.cloud.microsoft domain to maintain service reliability and avoid disruptions. 
  • Confirm that your environment aligns with the recommended network requirements for Microsoft 365 Copilot. 
  • Coordinate with teams that manage network security, proxy services, firewalls, secure web gateways, SSE/SASE platforms, or third-party filtering solutions to ensure traffic to *.cloud.microsoft is permitted. 
  • If preventing personal Microsoft account sign-ins is the reason your organization blocks copilot.cloud.microsoft, consider using TenantRestrictions as the targeted control. This control allows your organization to restrict authentication with personal Microsoft accounts on managed networks or devices, while still permitting access to the Copilot service URL.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Starting September 2026, Microsoft will redirect users from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft. Organizations must ensure network and security controls allow access to copilot.cloud.microsoft to avoid service disruption. Review and update firewall, proxy, and allow lists to permit *.cloud.microsoft traffic before October 2026.

Title: Allow connections to copilot.cloud.microsoft before the Copilot URL redirect

What and Why:

We're introducing a new reporting capability in Microsoft Agent 365 that enables AI Admins and Global Admins to export an inventory of users who have actively used agents registered in their tenant's Agent 365 Registry during the previous 30 days.

This report provides visibility into agent usage and can help organizations support agent licensing reviews and planning activities.

Rollout Schedule:

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rolling out in late August 2026 and expected to complete by late August 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected

  • AI Admins
  • Global Admins

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Agent 365

What will happen

A new Active Users export option will be available in:

Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All Agents > Export

Authorized administrators will be able to generate a CSV report containing users who have used an agent represented in the tenant's Agent 365 Registry during the previous 30 days.

The report includes:

  • User Principal Name (UPN)
  • Total Agents Used
  • Total Sessions
  • Last Activity Date

This is a read-only reporting capability.

There are no changes to:

  • Existing agents
  • User permissions
  • Billing processes

The feature will be enabled by default for AI Admins and Global Admins who already have access to Agent 365.

Action Required / Recommendations:

No action is required to prepare for this change.

After rollout, you may want to:

  • Identify the individuals responsible for agent licensing decisions and ensure they have the appropriate administrative access.
  • Review exported usage data to better understand agent adoption across your organization.
  • Use the report to support internal licensing reviews and planning discussions.

Compliance Considerations:

The feature introduces a new administrative reporting capability that exposes existing usage information for agent activity. The export includes user identifiers (UPN) and usage metrics for the previous 30 days. Organizations should review their internal policies regarding access to usage reporting data and retention of exported reports.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Agent 365 will add an Active Users export in the Microsoft 365 admin center, allowing AI and Global Admins to generate a CSV report of users who used agents in the past 30 days. This read-only feature aids licensing reviews and requires no preparation.

Title: Microsoft Agent 365: Active Users export for agent usage reporting

What and Why

Microsoft Teams is introducing AI generated meeting archive files that capture key insights from meetings. These archives help Microsoft 365 Copilot and Facilitator deliver more accurate context aware responses while maintaining strong privacy controls by not storing raw meeting content. This capability supports enterprise ready AI by improving knowledge grounding while keeping data secure and manageable.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558933.

Rollout Schedule

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early October 2026 (previously early September) and expected to complete mid-October 2026 (previously mid-September)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-October 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete late October 2026 (previously late September)

Teams admin center controls for this feature will be available approximately two weeks before archive file generation begins. The dates above reflect when admin controls become available.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams administrators
  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Facilitator capabilities enabled

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • SharePoint Embedded

What will happen

  • AI meeting archive files (.meeting files) will be generated for meetings where AI is turned on, one participant has a Copilot license, and transcription is enabled. The feature is enabled by default in your organization.
  • Archive files are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container, not in user storage. You can control the default expiration time for these files within your organization.
  • Users cannot directly view or access archive files.
  • When the feature is released, Facilitator will use the archive to answer questions about meetings and responses include citations linking to meeting recaps or invites. In the future, Copilot will also use the archive to answer questions about meetings. 
  • Archive files cannot be modified, renamed, or moved.
  • All content in archive files is AI-generated. No raw transcript snippets are stored.
  • Archive generation requires all of the following:
    • A meeting transcript is created and saved
    • At least one Copilot-licensed participant is invited
    • The meeting option "Allow Copilot and Facilitator" is set to "During and after the meeting"
  • Archive files are not created for:
    • Meetings with sensitivity labels that include encryption
    • End-to-end encrypted meetings
    • Meetings with restricted copying or forwarding
  • Access and data protection:
    • Only users with access to the meeting can receive responses grounded in its archive and AI tools do not surface insights to users who do not have meeting access.
    • Archive knowledge is only shared with users who are in the same tenant as the meeting organizer.

Action Required / Recommendations

No immediate action is required. However, administrators should review configuration settings and consider organizational policy alignment.

Admins can enable or disable this feature in the Teams admin center.

Recommended actions:

  • Review the AI archive setting in Teams admin center before rollout. Setting path: Meeting Policies > AI Memory and Archive > "Allow AI to archive meetings with .meeting file generation".
  • Evaluate the default expiration period, which is set to five years (1,825 days), and adjust retention settings as needed to align with compliance policies.
  • Communicate this capability to helpdesk teams and compliance stakeholders.
  • Monitor availability of the AI archive setting in Teams admin center and review or update settings when they become available. Archive file generation will begin 2 weeks after the setting is released to your organization.

Learn more: AI Archives for Microsoft Teams Meetings | Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn 

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data, and if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. The change introduces AI-generated meeting archive files that are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container and retained according to a configurable retention period.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Meeting transcripts and metadata are processed into structured AI archive files that enable downstream AI systems such as Copilot and Facilitator to reason over meeting content.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot and Facilitator use AI meeting archive files to generate context-aware responses grounded in prior meeting content.
Does the change provide users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Copilot and Facilitator, which leverage meeting archive data to answer questions and provide insights about meetings.
Does the change modify retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. AI meeting archive files are governed by a default retention period of five years and are automatically deleted upon expiration.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can enable or disable AI meeting archive generation and configure retention settings in the Teams Admin Center.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Teams will generate AI meeting archive files starting October 2026 to enhance Copilot and Facilitator responses. Archives store AI-generated insights (not raw content) in tenant-owned SharePoint, with admin controls for enabling, retention, and compliance. Users cannot access archives directly; data privacy and access are strictly managed.

Details.Name: Platforms
Details.Value: Web

Title: Microsoft Teams: AI meeting archive file generation

What and why:
The Windows Management Instrumentation command-line (WMIC) utility has been removed from Windows 11, version 24H2 and later. It’s no longer available as a Feature on Demand on these versions. WMI itself remains supported and unaffected.
 
Rollout schedule:
  • 2016: WMIC utility was deprecated in Windows Server 2012.
  • 2021: WMIC utility was deprecated in Windows 10, version 21H2.
  • 2022: WMIC utility was available in Windows 11, version 22H2 as a Feature on Demand (FoD), which was preinstalled and enabled by default.
  • 2024: WMIC utility was disabled by default in Windows 11, versions 23H2 and 24H2. It was still available as a Feature on Demand (FoD).
  • 2025: WMIC utility was removed, if already installed, when upgrading to Windows 11, version 25H2. However, you could previously add it back as a Feature on Demand (FoD).
  • 2026: The WMIC utility has been removed from Windows 11. The removal is reflected in Windows Insider Preview builds and is part of the August 2026 preview update for Windows 11, versions 24H2 and 25H2. WMIC is also removed from Windows 11, version 26H1. It is no longer available as a Feature on Demand (FoD).

Impact on your organization:
Organizations with automated deployment or monitoring systems that rely on WMIC should validate and update their tooling to avoid disruptions.
 
Action required/recommendations:
Organizations should identify applications, scripts, deployment tools, and monitoring systems that use WMIC and migrate them to PowerShell or supported WMI programming interfaces. Learn more at Windows Management Instrumentation command-line (WMIC) removal from Windows.
 
Compliance considerations:
No compliance considerations are identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

Title: Prepare for the removal of WMIC from Windows 11

The August 2026 non-security preview update is now available for Windows 11, versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2. Information about the contents of this update is available in the release notes, which are accessible from the Windows 11 update history page. To learn more about the different types of monthly quality updates, see Understanding Windows monthly updates.
 
Looking to explore upcoming features and improvements in Windows 11? Check the Windows roadmap. It includes what’s coming to the Windows Insider Program, what's gradually rolling out, and what's generally available.
 
Highlights for the Windows 11, version 25H2 update:
  • You can now choose whether the taskbar appears at the bottom, top, left, or right side of your screen, with tooltips, flyouts, and most customization settings, such as never combining taskbar icons, working in every position.
  • A new smaller taskbar option reduces the size of taskbar icons and taskbar height to maximize screen space on smaller devices, while keeping quick access to Start, Search, and the system tray.
  • The Start menu is now more personal, letting you choose a small or large menu size, independently show or hide the Pinned, Recommended, and All sections, and hide your name and profile picture.
  • Windows Search now makes results easier to scan by showing where each result comes from—app, setting, file, web, or Store—and can automatically index your most used folders so those files show up in your searches.
  • Launching File Explorer Home is now faster and more responsive, and the Recommended section supports touch scrolling for easier browsing.
  • Administrator protection helps reduce the risk of elevation-of-privilege attacks by using profile separation and just-in-time administrative privileges. It is off by default and can be enabled through Microsoft Intune (OMA-URI) or Group Policy.
 
For instructions on how to install this update, see the KB article for your operating system listed below:
  • Windows 11, version 26H1: KB5120996
  • Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2: KB5120998

This one‑time restart occurs after a Secure Boot certificate update is applied as part of the Secure Boot update process.

Introduction

To support more effective in-person collaboration, Microsoft Teams is expanding AI-powered meeting notes with the Facilitator agent to Teams Rooms on Windows. This enhancement allows teams meeting in a physical room to capture real-time notes, decisions, and action items—without requiring a scheduled or hybrid meeting. The experience is designed to ensure notes are securely stored in your tenant while no data remains on the room device after the meeting ends.

This feature is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 560318.

When this will happen

General Availability

  • Worldwide and GCC: We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 (previously early September) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late September).

How this affects your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Teams Rooms on Windows
  • Rooms licensed with Teams Rooms Pro

What will happen

  • During an in-person meeting, users can start AI-powered notes by selecting the Take notes button on the Teams Rooms console.
  • Notes appear on the front-of-room display or touch board during the meeting: 

  • Notes are stored in tenant-owned SharePoint embedded storage.

  • Access to notes requires adding your work account using the Access notes button on the Teams Rooms console: 

  • After the meeting, notes can be viewed and edited by participants with access via the meeting recap in the meeting chat on the Teams desktop client.:
  • If no participant was added during the note-taking session via Access notes, notes are deleted automatically.

Default state:

  • The feature is available automatically once licensing and prerequisite configurations are met.
  • No additional admin enablement is required beyond existing settings.

What you can do to prepare

No immediate action is required if your organization already meets the prerequisites.

To prepare:

  • Confirm Teams Rooms Pro licenses are assigned to applicable rooms.
  • Ensure Facilitator is enabled in your tenant.
  • Verify Loop components are enabled:
    • IsLoopEnabled
    • IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled
  • Ensure meeting transcription is enabled in Teams meeting policies.
  • Consider notifying helpdesk staff and users about:
    • How to start notes in an in-person meeting
    • Where notes are stored and accessed after the meeting

Learn more:

  • Allow Facilitator in the Teams admin center - Set up Facilitator in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Meetings - Admins- Manage transcription and captions for Teams meetings | Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Settings management for Loop functionality in Teams - Admin policies for Loop components and Loop workspaces | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data, and if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. Meeting notes generated by Facilitator are stored in tenant‑owned SharePoint Embedded storage. No meeting data is stored or cached on the Teams Rooms device after the meeting ends.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (for example, documents, emails, or chats)?Yes. Meeting audio and transcription data are processed to generate AI‑powered meeting notes, including summaries, decisions, and action items. Access to the notes occurs through the meeting recap in the meeting chat on Teams desktop client.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The Facilitator agent uses AI to generate real‑time meeting notes, summaries, decisions, and action items based on in‑person meeting content.
Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI, and if so, how?Yes. Users can initiate AI‑generated meeting notes during an in‑person meeting by selecting “Take notes” on the Teams Rooms console.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through tenant configuration?Yes. Availability of the feature depends on existing tenant settings, including Teams Rooms Pro licensing, Facilitator enablement, Loop component settings, and meeting transcription policies.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Teams is adding AI-powered meeting notes with the Facilitator agent to Teams Rooms on Windows for in-person meetings. Rolling out worldwide from late October to mid-November 2026, it enables real-time note-taking stored securely in tenant-owned SharePoint. Licensing and configuration prerequisites apply; no extra admin enablement needed.

Details.Name: Platforms
Details.Value: TeamsAndSurfaceDevices

Title: Microsoft Teams: AI-powered notes for in-person meetings with Facilitator in Teams Rooms on Windows

Introduction

Adaptive scopes for SharePoint DLP policies in Microsoft Purview enable you to target SharePoint sites based on site attributes instead of manually maintaining static site lists. As sites are created or updated, adaptive scopes automatically adjust membership, ensuring that DLP policies remain aligned to your environment without ongoing manual updates.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 549288.

When this will happen

  • Public Preview: We began rollout in early February 2026 and expect to complete by late‑February 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rollout in early January 2027 (previously late August 2026) and expect to complete by late January 2027 (previously late September).

How this will affect your organization

Who is affected: Admins who manage Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies for SharePoint in Microsoft Purview.

What will happen:

With adaptive scopes for SharePoint, your organization will -

  • Apply DLP policies more efficiently and at scale.
  • Automatically target the correct SharePoint sites based on attributes such as URL, name, or metadata.
  • Ensure new or updated sites are protected without manual list maintenance.
  • Reduce administrative overhead by removing the need to maintain static site lists.
  • Maintain consistent DLP policy coverage as your SharePoint environment grows and changes.

Additional notes:

  • There is no impact to user workflows.
  • The feature is not enabled by default; admins must create and assign adaptive scopes.

What you can do to prepare

To prepare for this update, you can:

  • Verify licensing and permissions.
  • Ensure your tenant has Microsoft 365 E5 or E5 Compliance licensing and that you hold the required Purview roles.
  • Learn more: Configure adaptive scopes - Adaptive Scopes | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn
  • Navigate to Adaptive scopes.
  • Go to Microsoft Purview compliance portal → Settings → Roles & scopes → Adaptive scopes (screenshot 1):

  • Create an adaptive scope.
  • Select + Create scope.
  • Provide a name and description.
  • Choose SharePoint sites as the scope type (screenshot 2):

  • Define the scope criteria.
  • Use the query builder to set rules based on SharePoint site attributes such as:
    • Site URL
    • Site name
    • Custom metadata
  • Review and create the scope.
  • Confirm your criteria and create the scope. The system evaluates and updates scope membership automatically.
  • Verify scope membership.
  • Review included sites using the Adaptive scopes details pane (screenshot 3):

  • Apply the scope to a DLP policy.
  • When creating or editing a SharePoint DLP policy, select your adaptive scope (screenshots 4 and 5):

    .

  • Allow time for periodic evaluation.
  • Changes to adaptive scopes may take time to reflect across applied policies.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Purview introduces adaptive scopes for SharePoint DLP policies, enabling automatic targeting of sites based on attributes, reducing manual updates. Public preview runs February 2026; general availability begins January 2027. Admins must create scopes and assign them to DLP policies to improve efficiency and coverage without impacting user workflows.

We are announcing the ability to use real-time web tracking and personalization for known and unknown users in Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Data. This feature will reach general availability on September 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature enables two key capabilities: website personalization for known and unknown users, as well as conversion of unknown users to known users.
  • Track unknown user activity. When users return to your site, personalize it based on their previous browsing behavior on your site.
  • Personalize your website using a pro-code API-driven approach for experienced development teams or use built-in integration with Optimizely to personalize your site using a no-code approach.
  • When an unknown user provides you with contactable details like an email address or phone number, you can convert the unknown user into a known profile that persists the tracked activity data from when they were an unknown user.
What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Real-time web tracking and personalization for known and unknown users.

Title: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Data - Real-time web tracking and personalization for known and unknown users

We are announcing the ability to enable multiple eliminations for an investment project in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. This feature will reach public preview on September 11, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature removes the restriction on only a single elimination transaction being permitted per investment project. With this change, finance and project accountants can post multiple elimination transactions against a single investment project—supporting staged capitalization, cost overruns, and partial expense scenarios.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required. If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Enable multiple eliminations for an investment project.

Title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations- Enable multiple eliminations for an investment project

Body.Content:
We are announcing the ability to unify product receipt and item requirement posting in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. This feature will reach public preview on September 11, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature posts a purchase order product receipt and the consumption of its linked project item requirement in one transaction. It applies when automatic item consumption is enabled or when you select "Consume immediately" while posting the product receipt. Both updates succeed together, or the system rolls them both back when an error occurs. The posting flow prevents duplicate project posting and preserves existing behavior for batch posting and cancellation or correction flows. This combined posting can only be triggered from the product receipt posting.

This feature applies to the Project Operations Integrated with ERP and Project Operations for manufacturing deployment types.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Unify product receipt and item requirement posting.

Title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations - Unify product receipt and item requirement posting

Body.Content:
We are announcing the ability to post costs for manual transfer from the balance sheet in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. This feature will reach public preview on September 11, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Organizations may have long running work for internal initiatives or customer facing projects. When cost and revenue profile rules are configured to post costs to the balance sheet (for example, as work in progress assets), there's a point when those costs must be recognized as expenses. At that time, the amounts are reclassified from the balance sheet to the profit and loss statement.

This feature enables manual movement of costs between the balance sheet and profit and loss statements. Enhancements include:
  • A new Post costs form to view, select, and perform posting.
  • Allowing users to select a single transaction or multiple transactions filtered by transaction date and transaction type (expense, hour, or item).
This feature is specific to customers using the Project Operations Integrated with ERP deployment type.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Post costs for manual transfer from the balance sheet.

Title: Dynamics 365 Project Operations - Post costs for manual transfer from the balance sheet

What and why:

We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default. At the center of this update is a new hero link—a single sharing link that controls access to a file or folder.

Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL.   • General Availability (Worldwide): Rolling out mid-September 2026 (previously late August) through late October 2026
  • GCC: Rolling out mid-September 2026 (previously late August) through late October 2026
  • GCC High: Rolling out mid-September 2026 (previously late August) through late October 2026
  • DoD: Rolling out mid-September 2026 (previously late August) through late October 2026

Impact on your organization:

Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365.

Platforms and services: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 file-sharing experiences.

What will happen:

  • Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.
  • The hero link settings determine who can access the item beyond people who are explicitly granted access.
  • Adding people directly to a file or folder remains unchanged and continues to be the simplest way to share content.

Screenshot - Add people screen when sharing 

  • By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

Screenshot - Share file view with hero link

  • Users can broaden access to people in the organization with the link or, where permitted by organizational policy, to anyone with the link.
  • Users can choose whether recipients can view, edit, or view without downloading, depending on available permissions.
  • Changing the audience for the hero link updates the existing link rather than creating a new one.
  • If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.
  • Existing sharing links will continue to function and will appear under Other links in the sharing dialog.
  • Effective access remains the most permissive combination of direct permissions, inherited permissions, group-based permissions, and link-based permissions.
  • Users will see a tutorial experience upon opening the new share dialog for the first time.

Action required/Recommendations:

No action is required before rollout.

Organizations should consider the following preparation activities:

  • Review internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation to reflect the new single-link sharing model.
  • Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.
  • Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.

Learn more:

  • Walkthrough Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3RpE0KrQmcA&t=4s
  • Announcement Blog: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/onedriveblog/simple-smart-and-secure-the-next-step-in-sharing-files-in-microsoft-365/4411655

Admin controls

  • Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.
  • Supported values are:
    • OnlyPeopleAdded (default)
    • Organization
  • There is currently no tenant-wide equivalent setting for the hero link audience.
  • DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.
  • Hero links start with view permissions by default.
  • Existing default sharing link settings and link expiration policies continue to apply to legacy links and do not govern hero links.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

Details.Value: Microsoft 365 introduces a third-generation sharing experience with a single "hero link" for files and folders, simplifying access control and updates. Rolling out worldwide from mid-September to late October 2026, it affects SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 sharing, with no required user action before rollout.

What and why

Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is updating the Microsoft Entra roles that grant access to App Governance when Unified Role-Based Access Control (URBAC) is enabled. As part of this change, support for the Cloud Application Administrator role will be retired for App Governance access.

This change aligns App Governance access with the standard supported role set used across Microsoft Defender services and supports future role-based access enhancements.

Rollout schedule

  • Retirement (Worldwide): Beginning in late September 2026
  • Enforcement date: September 26, 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations that use App Governance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and have administrators who access App Governance using only the Cloud Application Administrator Microsoft Entra role

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
  • App Governance
  • Microsoft Entra ID

What will happen

After September 26, 2026:

  • Administrators assigned only the Cloud Application Administrator role will no longer be able to access App Governance when URBAC is enabled for Defender for Cloud Apps.
  • Administrators assigned one of the supported roles will continue to have access based on their permissions.
  • No user experience changes are expected.

Action required and recommendations

Review administrator assignments by September 25, 2026.

Assign an appropriate supported role to any administrator who requires App Governance access. Supported roles include:

  • Security Administrator
  • Compliance Administrator
  • Compliance Data Administrator
  • Security Operator
  • Security Reader
  • Application Administrator
  • Global Reader

We recommend assigning the role with the minimum permissions required for each administrator's responsibilities.

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does this change modify administrative access to a Microsoft 365 service?Yes. This change removes App Governance access for administrators who are assigned only the Cloud Application Administrator Microsoft Entra role when URBAC is enabled for Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
Does this change require organizations to review or update role assignments?Yes. Organizations should review current administrator role assignments and assign a supported role to administrators who require App Governance access before September 26, 2026.
Does this change affect how administrators control or access the service?Yes. Access to App Governance will be governed by a revised set of supported Microsoft Entra roles, changing how some administrators obtain access to the service.
Does this change involve an administrative control or permissions change?Yes. The change retires support for one administrative role and requires use of one of the supported roles to maintain App Governance access.

What and Why:

We're excited to introduce an org-wide single pane for monitoring and troubleshooting meetings and calls in the Teams admin center. IT administrators will be able to find all the meetings and calls in one place, get quick insights, and get started with troubleshooting right away. 

 The new experience helps administrators: 

  1. View in-progress and completed meetings across the organization from a single location.
  2. Quickly identify meetings that may require attention. 
  3. Search for meetings using meeting identifiers and other filters. 


Rollout Schedule:

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by mid October 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC): Rollout will begin in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by mid October 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected

  • Teams administrators responsible for monitoring and troubleshooting meeting and call quality across their organization.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams admin center

What will happen

After rollout, administrators will see a new Meetings experience in the Teams admin center under Meetings & Calls.

  • Navigate to Teams admin center > Meetings & Calls > Meetings or Calls to access the updated troubleshooting experience.
  • View and monitor meetings across the organization from a centralized Meetings experience.
  • Review both in-progress and completed meetings, search for specific meetings, apply filters, and open meeting details for troubleshooting.
  • Review completed calls across the organization to identify and troubleshoot call quality issues.

Available capabilities include:

  • In-progress meetings: View meetings, town halls, and webinars currently occurring in the organization when at least one participant has a Teams Premium license or Teams Rooms Pro license.
  • Completed meetings: View meetings that occurred across the organization during the previous 30 days.

  • Completed calls: Review completed calls across the organization to investigate call quality issues.

  • Issue details: Quickly identify issues experienced by participants and access additional details.
  • Detailed diagnostics: Drill down into telemetry and diagnostic information to support root cause analysis and troubleshooting.
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot for Admins: Use Copilot to investigate individual meetings or analyze trends across the organization.
  • Filtering and search: Refine results using filters such as:
    • Time range (last 7 days, 15 days, 30 days, or a custom date range)
    • Meetings with issues
    • Organizer
    • Meeting type
    • Additional meeting and participant attributes
  • Export: Export meeting and call data for offline analysis, reporting, and investigation.

Action Required / Recommendations:

No action is required. The updated experience will be available automatically after rollout. Once available, administrators can begin using the new capabilities to monitor and troubleshoot meetings and calls across their organization.

Compliance Considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
